counting_rules: One family per distinct score, balance, load, energy estimate or recommendation output; daily/workout aliases and presentation variants deduplicated.

Includes separately displayed Sleep Bank, Consistency, Needed, Target Strain and HR Recovery, plus Daily Nutrition and Muscular Load. This intentionally replaces the arbitrary earlier 11-headline grouping.
ATL/CTL/TRIMP/cardio optimal ranges belong to Cardio Load. Age groups, PhenoAge, factor impacts, confidence and projection belong to Biological Age. Stress contexts are one Stress family.

Food Quality, Food Glucose and overall Daily Nutrition are separate outputs. Per-muscle and overall freshness are one family. Cardio Focus is a workout contribution/dimension summary, excluded from score-family count.
Raw measurements, macro balance breakdown, strength helpers, journal regression/results and cycle predictions remain inventoried but excluded from scalar score/balance/recommendation count.

11 mapped-core candidates means input plausibility for cardio/sleep/HR fallback branches plus profile/settings, not full Air pipeline proof. Biological Age adds one partial composite, making 12 counterpart benchmark targets.
Two new cardio-only leads are Muscular Load and Freshness; their source conversion/eligibility is untraced. They are neither proven new Air-compatible algorithms nor established impossible.

Four additional-input families are Food Glucose, Food Quality, Daily Nutrition and personalized TDEE. TDEE has numeric fallback branches; fallback availability does not establish personalized parity. Biological Age and full strength models have extra data gaps outside their Air branches.
Counts describe discovered outputs, not exhaustive app completeness. No runtime input/output validation exists.
Imported Oura readiness, EPOC/TRIMP series, setting enums, errors, calibration states and cached record fields are inputs or internal models, not extra Bevel score families.

heart_rate_recovery.formula: For chronological finite input points, select minimum(HR[j]-HR[k]) over earlier k<j with time[j]-time[k]<=120 seconds and time[k]<=activeWorkoutEnd. Service converts delta to Float32 then negates it.
heart_rate_recovery.implementation: Sliding maximum-HR deque for eligible earlier points; minimum delta across later points. Helper does not sort input.
heart_rate_recovery.comparison_evidence: 0x1017cdd80-0x1017cdd98 evicts window-ineligible starts; 0x1017cdda0-0x1017cdda4 skips inserting points after activeWorkoutEnd; 0x1017cde68-0x1017cde90 selects strictly smaller delta; 0x1017cd8e0-0x1017cd8e4 converts and negates.
heart_rate_recovery.null_behavior: Selector returns nil for fewer than two points, window <= 0, or no eligible pair. Full service eligibility and errors remain partial.
heart_rate_recovery.clipping: No numeric drop clipping observed in these local functions; increasing HR can yield negative recovery.
heart_rate_recovery.time_semantics: No local requirement that the later point is after activeWorkoutEnd. Upstream supplied interval is essential; this is not proven to be a fixed two-minute post-workout measurement.
